images.filename: StateLibQld 2 390817 Horsedrawn tram on St. Helena Island, 1928.jpg
images.caption:
Horsedrawn tram on St. Helena Island, 1928
The horsedrawn tram was used to transport people from the causeway jetty to the prison buildings on the hill. The tram ran on 3'6' guage tracks. Many of the track rails can be seen on the island but have been used as reinforcing for concrete covers on some of the large wells. (Description supplied with photograph.).
images.alt:
Horsedrawn tram on St. Helena Island, 1928
The horsedrawn tram was used to transport people from the causeway jetty to the prison buildings on the hill. The tram ran on 3'6' guage tracks. images.filename: StateLibQld 2 293323 Prisoners making uniforms in the tailors' workshop on St Helena Island, 1911.jpg
images.caption:
Prisoners making uniforms in the tailors' workshop on St Helena Island, 1911
The tailors' workshop where prison uniforms, police uniforms and any other necessary sewing was done by the convicts. Notice the tailors on the side benches are all sitting cross-legged with the material to be sewn lying across their knees. This was the position used by all tailors in the days of hand tailoring. (Description supplied with photograph.).
images.alt:
Prisoners making uniforms in the tailors' workshop on St Helena Island, 1911
The tailors' workshop where prison uniforms, police uniforms and any other necessary sewing was done by the convicts. images.filename: StateLibQld 2 392393 Signal cannon on St. Helena Island, 1939.jpg
images.caption:
Signal cannon on St. Helena Island, 1939
This cannon was kept on the island as a tool of warning to any vessels like fishing boats or pleasure craft which seemed to sail too close to the prison. A warning shot would be fired in the general direction of the offending vessel. The cannon is now the property of the Stafford district boy scouts and is standing at their hall. (Description supplied with photograph.).
images.alt:
Signal cannon on St. Helena Island, 1939

images.filename: StateLibQld 2 392577 Vegetable gardens, H.M. Penal Establishment, St. Helena (Prisioners' garden in foreground), 1911.jpg
images.caption:
Vegetable gardens, H.M. Penal Establishment, St. Helena (Prisioners' garden in foreground), 1911
The vegetable garden was quite large, supplying the island's needs. Through most of the life of this island prison, the jail was self-supporting. In fact, during most years a profit was shown on the balance sheet. Water was brought from the wells and then poured over the plants by hand-held watering cans. (Description supplied with photograph).
images.alt:
Vegetable gardens, H.M. Penal Establishment, St. Helena (Prisioners' garden in foreground), 1911

images.filename: StateLibQld 2 390813 Ornate fountain on St. Helena Island, 1928.jpg
images.caption:
Ornate fountain on St. Helena Island, 1928.
One of the ornate fountains near the rear of the superintendants's house. When first constructed the fountains blew water high into the sky. To achieve this, selected prisoners were hidden over the edge of a steep bank on the north side of the island. Here a pump was worked vigorously up and down to force water through the fountain jets. The fountain is made of coral. (Description supplied with photograph.).
images.alt:
Ornate fountain on St. Helena Island, 1928.
One of the ornate fountains near the rear of the superintendants's house. When first constructed the fountains blew water high into the sky.
